summary: Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a B.A. from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Radcliffe College and Harvard University (Ph.D. ~1973), she held professorships at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (2004).

Pierce Salguero specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. Educated at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (Ph.D. ~2010), he was appointed professor of Asian History and Health Humanities at Penn State Abington around 2010.
Pierre Arènes works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under André Bareau and held an attested post at the CNRS from 2003 to 2004.

Pierre Bourdieu was a French scholar of philosophy and other fields. He studied under Émile Benveniste and at the École Normale Supérieure, later holding posts at EHESS (1975) and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine was a French linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between ~1920 and ~1927. He later held a post at the University of Paris from ~1938 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry and EFEO (~1963–1967), held the Chair of Sanskrit at the EPHE (1967–2004), and was President of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (2010).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University by 1991, where he was also attested as a Research-Fellow in 1996.
Pieter Hendrik Pott was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology/history. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (~1940–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin in 1867. He later held academic posts at the University of Pavia, becoming an ordinary professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.

Piotr Balcerowicz is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Warsaw and the University of Hamburg (Dr. phil. 1999) and has served as a professor of Indology at the University of Warsaw since ~2000.

Piotr Klafkowski was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski, and studied under traditional teachers including Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.
Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Palzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom (~1920–1926) and later served as a professor at Gadjah Mada University and the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964).

Polly Young-Eisendrath works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Washington University in St. Louis, underwent Zen training under Philip Kapleau and Shinzen Young, and became a clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont (1994).

Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He held positions as State Engineer for Junagadh, Chief Engineer for Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for the Hyderabad Municipality.
Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Robert Buswell. She has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Potprecha Cholvijarn works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Chulalongkorn University and the University of Bristol, completed his doctoral studies under Rupert Gethin, and served as a special lecturer at Chulalongkorn University (attested 2011).
Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).
Prabhasa Dharma was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teachers Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (from 1967) and Seikō Hirata.
